argument_summary: The present record supports certification only in a qualified form. Admissible evidence shows aggregate readiness clears the launch bar and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which is enough to defend launch readiness at the overall model level. The same record also shows an unresolved below-target slice in long-context small-business onboarding and only a draft runbook with owner and threshold still TBD. That combination does not support a clean, caveat-free certification packet. It does support certification with explicit disclosure of the limitation in the model card and with the runbook characterized as draft monitoring support rather than an approved mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not the basis for the policy conclusion. The narrower compliance treatment also avoids unnecessary escalation if the auditor agrees the evidence supports a disclosed-limitation posture rather than a failed-certification posture.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is narrower than a blanket bar on certification. It says certification without material caveats requires either no remaining material weakness or an approved mitigation containing owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible record does not show those approval elements, so the draft runbook cannot erase any disclosure obligation by itself. At the same time, the policy does not require treating the entire launch as noncompliant if the issue is handled as a disclosed limitation rather than as a closed mitigation. The supportable policy position is caveated compliance, not clean compliance.
concessions: The current record does not prove an approved mitigation or approved risk acceptance.

The current record does not directly establish, as a formal adjudicated fact, that the small-business onboarding issue has already been classified as a material limitation for a named launch use case.
A clean certification conclusion would overstate what the admissible evidence supports.
